sense.text: Who is Esau? This is where it starts: “these are the generations of Isaac, Abraham’s son”. Isaac was forty years old when he took Rebekah to wife, the daughter of Bethuel the Syrian of Padan–aram.

Rebekah was barren; she could not have children. So Isaac “intreated the Lord for his wife”: he prayed for his wife, as all husbands should be praying for their wives. The Lord heard that prayer, “and Rebekah his wife conceived.”

“The children struggled together within her”, so much that she said, “If it be so, why am I thus?” If pregnancy is like this, how am I still alive? There was a lot of pain going on in there. So “she went to enquire of the Lord”: she went to pray to the Lord about it.

“Two nations are in thy womb, and two manner of people shall be separated from thy bowels.” With that alone you know these children are not the same. They are in the same womb, but they are two different types of children, two different nations.

“The one people shall be stronger than the other people”: that one people is us, the so-called blacks, Latinos and Native Americans who are under the branch of Jacob, the chosen line.

“The elder shall serve the younger”: the first child that comes out is the eldest, and that child is going to serve the second child, the stronger one.

There were twins in her womb, “And the first came out red, all over like an hairy garment; and they called his name Esau.” The first child, they went right into detail: this is a white child, a Slavic baby, rice-skinned, but with red all over it. He was red; you could see the blood showing through his skin. The picture of Esau the cunning hunter shows it.

“And after that came his brother out, and his hand took hold on Esau’s heel; and his name was called Jacob.” The second child is not described. They did not explain what Jacob looked like, because he was a normal child: the children normally came out black, with healthy skin.

precepts.why:
This is why the birth of Jacob and Esau matters; Esdras tells what the whole purpose of that birth was. Esdras asks, “What shall be the parting asunder of the times? or when shall be the end of the first, and the beginning of it that followeth?” In other words: when is it that we will be in rulership, when will we be on top? When is the end of what we are going through right now, and when does your kingdom begin, Lord?

The answer goes straight back to the birth: “From Abraham unto Isaac, when Jacob and Esau were born of him, Jacob’s hand held first the heel of Esau.” The birth was a prophecy. Esau is the first, the elder, and he gets his run of the blessings first.

“For Esau is the end of the world, and Jacob is the beginning of it that followeth.” Esau is the last ruling empire. After Esau has had his run of the blessings, our blessings take place, and they are forever: that is the everlasting kingdom under Christ.

“The hand of man is betwixt the heel and the hand”: there is some stuff that is going to go down in between, and then we get into the kingdom. After that the angel said, “other question, Esdras, ask thou not”: don’t ask any more, I know where you are going with that question and I am giving you no more answers.

sense.text:
How did Esau become the greatly despised? How is it that the Lord greatly despised him? Because he is the one that hated first.

“Esau was a cunning hunter, a man of the field”: look at the image of him, a demon. “And Jacob was a plain man, dwelling in tents”: a plain brother. He wasn’t all that, just a plain brother.

“Isaac loved Esau, because he did eat of his venison”: Esau knew how to cook that deer. “But Rebekah loved Jacob”, because Rebekah knew something Isaac didn’t. When she went to enquire of the Lord, the Lord told her there were two nations in her womb, two manner of people, that one would be stronger than the other and the elder would serve the younger. How was this going to happen? Only Rebekah knew, because of what the Lord had told her.

Esau came from the field faint and said, “Feed me, I pray thee, with that same red pottage”. That red pottage had red meat in it, and it wasn’t cooked all the way. That is what so-called white people do: they like their meat medium rare, or rare, or tartar, which is raw. This is not a personal class; it is showing why they are greatly despised. Biting into straight animal muscle, like the caveman.

“For I am faint”: he was about to die. “Therefore was his name called Edom.” Edom means red.

The bishop already brought out the receipts in Modern Judaism (1830): the rabbis’ own traditions hold that the descendants of Esau are the sworn enemies of the descendants of Jacob, which is us, even to the end of the world. They will never be your friend. To hell with Miss Laura, to hell with Señor Bob: they don’t love you. They were at first a small nation inhabiting Mount Seir and the country around it. Remember that name, Mount Seir.

The same book says that as long as Israel had its empire in Canaan they stayed small, but after the twelve tribes were destroyed by the Assyrians and Babylonians, meaning when we went into slavery, Esau wonderfully increased, extended his dominion west, subjugated Italy, founded Rome and the Roman Empire, and overturned the Jewish state, the second temple being destroyed by Titus Vespasian. They hold dominion over all Europe, Esau detaining his brother Jacob in captivity.

It says too that the prophecies against Esau, Edom, Seir and the cities of Edom, especially those of Isaiah, Jeremiah and Obadiah, have not yet received their full accomplishment: we are in the middle of identifying who these people are. Those plagues belong to Rome and the Christians. Rome, where the Vatican City is, is inhabited by the same people who hate Jacob, the so-called blacks, Latinos and Native Americans today. And of them Obadiah says there shall not be any remaining of the house of Esau: that is future judgment.

Jacob said, “Sell me this day thy birthright.” Esau said, “Behold, I am at the point to die: and what profit shall this birthright do to me?” I don’t give a damn about my birthright; let me get some of that red stuff in the pot. Jacob said, “Swear to me this day; and he sware unto him: and he sold his birthright unto Jacob.” Right there, Esau did not want his birthright. He just wanted that bowl of meat.
Jacob gave him bread and pottage of lentiles, and he ate and drank and went his way: “thus Esau despised his birthright.” That is what happened. Esau despised his birthright.

Isaac was old, “his eyes were dim, so that he could not see”, and he did not know the day of his death. He was about to die, and he wanted Esau to take his weapons, go to the field, take venison and make him savoury meat “such as I love”: hook him up with some meat before he died. He wanted to be comforted, “that my soul may bless thee before I die.”

Rebekah heard Isaac speak to Esau, and told Jacob, “obey my voice according to that which I command thee”: fetch two good kids of the goats, and she would make savoury meat for his father, “that he may bless thee before his death.”

Christians usually read this and blame Jacob. They say Jacob was wicked, that he lied, that he stole Esau’s birthright. That didn’t happen. Esau despised his birthright; he sold it for a bowl of meat.

Look what Jacob did. “Esau my brother is a hairy man, and I am a smooth man: My father peradventure will feel me, and I shall seem to him as a deceiver; and I shall bring a curse upon me, and not a blessing.” Jacob is not at fault here, because he tried. He said, I don’t want to do this, I don’t want to lie to my dad.

“Upon me be thy curse, my son: only obey my voice”: listen, I’m your mother, just do what I say. Why would she say that? Because she knew the prophecy. This is the moment where the elder shall serve the younger; this is what God told her years ago when the babies were in her womb.

Rebekah made it happen. She said, in effect, you are going to commit the sin, but don’t worry about it, I’ll pay for the sin. I know what God wants. Let it be on me.

She took “goodly raiment of her eldest son Esau” and put it on Jacob, because she wanted him to smell like Esau. When you have your hunting clothes on in the field, you get that smell, the wood smell, the tree smell, that earthy smell. And she put the skins of the kids of the goats on his hands and on the smooth of his neck.
“I am Esau thy firstborn”: he did exactly what his mother told him. Give him this food and act like your brother.

“How is it that thou hast found it so quickly, my son?” Isaac isn’t stupid. Hunting venison takes time: first you have to find the tracks to know it is even around, then you track it, then you wait, making sure you make no noise to scare it away.

“Because the Lord thy God brought it to me.” That is the way you answer. All praise to the Most High.

“Come near, I pray thee, that I may feel thee”: he still doubted; he wasn’t sure. “The voice is Jacob’s voice, but the hands are the hands of Esau.” He’s not dumb; he thought, maybe it’s my age, maybe I’m not too sharp anymore. Esau was a damn hairy boy; that hairy ass boy, Esau. “And he discerned him not, because his hands were hairy”: it sounded like Jacob but felt like Esau, and he couldn’t tell. “So he blessed him”: this is where the blessing comes.
“Art thou my very son Esau?” He was checking again: I don’t want to mess this up; you sound like Jacob but you feel like Esau. “And he said, I am.”

He ate and drank and was satisfied. Then “Come near now, and kiss me, my son”, because he wanted to smell him. All these little nuances were how he was testing: feel his hands, then kiss him to smell him, because he was still worried. “He smelled the smell of his raiment”, and there it was: “the smell of my son is as the smell of a field which the Lord hath blessed.” You smell like the earth, like a tree, like the field.

Here the prophecy goes according to what God wanted. God said the elder shall serve the younger. How is the elder going to serve the younger if the elder gets all of the blessings? Isaac loved Esau, and if you love your first boy you want to give that first one everything. But the Lord put it on Isaac to get dim eyes so that he could not discern, and that was when Rebekah saw her chance: put the younger son in as the elder so that he gets the elder’s blessings.

“Let people serve thee”: people, Esau included, are to serve Jacob. “And nations bow down to thee”: everyone bows down to you. “Be lord over thy brethren”, and “cursed be every one that curseth thee, and blessed be he that blesseth thee.” That is the blessing Jacob got. All of us have this blessing, but our blessing does not come into fruition until Esau has had his run.

As soon as Jacob was gone out, Esau came in from his hunting with his savoury meat, “I am thy son, thy firstborn Esau.” “And Isaac trembled very exceedingly”: a man came in here sounding like Jacob, smelling like you, feeling like you; you mean I blessed some other guy? Whatever I told him, he is going to get it: “yea, and he shall be blessed.” Jacob is going to be blessed.

Esau “cried with a great and exceeding bitter cry”, “Bless me, even me also, O my father.” “Thy brother came with subtilty, and hath taken away thy blessing.”

“Is not he rightly named Jacob? for he hath supplanted me these two times.” That is the name of Jacob: Jacob is a supplanter. Why two times? Don’t forget about the birthright, and then this moment right here.

“Behold, I have made him thy lord”: I have made your younger brother your lord. That is how the elder shall serve the younger. “All his brethren have I given to him for servants; and with corn and wine have I sustained him: and what shall I do now unto thee, my son?”
“Hast thou but one blessing, my father?” You don’t have anything left for me? “And Esau lifted up his voice, and wept.” This is the beginning of the hatred for Jacob.

Here is the blessing Esau has today. “Thy dwelling shall be the fatness of the earth”: they would conquer nations and have the best lands, and whatever lands were not in their possession, they would find a way to get. “And of the dew of heaven from above”: like early in the morning, when it is as if someone turned on the sprinkler and everything is cold and wet.

“And by thy sword shalt thou live”: by the sword is how Esau, Edom, Idumea live. They live fighting. This is what white people do: they fight everywhere. They go into the land, talk to you a little while, and when they don’t like the way the talk is going, they start cutting off heads, hands and legs.

“And shalt serve thy brother”: at the end of everything, you serve your brother. In effect Isaac was saying: I am giving you the blessings I gave Jacob, but limited. You are my favorite and I love you, but you know what your brother did. You are going to play with his blessing for a little while, and after that you serve your brother for the rest of your life. The toys I gave your brother you get first, but you give them back, and he has them forever.

“When thou shalt have the dominion”: when you become the world superpower in the earth. “That thou shalt break his yoke from off thy neck”: after you take him out of slavery.

“And Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing wherewith his father blessed him.” He didn’t like that blessing: everything you give me has a limit; I’m your son, your eldest; why should my blessing have a limit? It should be forever. No, because God said it, and it is a wrap. God’s will will be done.

“The days of mourning for my father are at hand; then will I slay my brother Jacob.” Once my father dies, I’m going after Jacob; I am sick and tired of Jacob. From there, this is the beginning of Esau’s perpetual hatred.

precepts.why:
Go back to see the first time Jacob supplanted him: “Feed me, I pray thee, with that same red pottage; for I am faint: therefore was his name called Edom.” His name was called Edom, and Edom means red.

That was the first of the “two times”: the birthright Esau sold for the red pottage. The second is the blessing taken in Genesis 27. That is why Esau says Jacob supplanted him twice.

Esau sought his blessing afterward with tears. “Looking diligently lest any man fail of the grace of God”: how can a man fail of the grace of God? When he despises God. When God says something and you refuse to do it, that is how you fall from the grace of God. What did Esau do? He despised his birthright.

“Lest any root of bitterness springing up trouble you”: Esau became bitter after that. He called his brother a supplanter: he got me twice, for my birthright and for my blessing. “And thereby many be defiled”: that is how Esau became defiled.

“Lest there be any fornicator, or profane person, as Esau”: Esau in the world is a fornicator and a profane person, “who for one morsel of meat sold his birthright.” For one spoonful of meat. It was not taken away from him; he sold it.

“For ye know how that afterward, when he would have inherited the blessing, he was rejected”, because the blessing went to his brother. The elder shall serve the younger. You can’t go around what God said; Rebekah made it happen.

“For he found no place of repentance, though he sought it carefully with tears.” He wept in front of his father, “Hast thou but one blessing, my father?”, but it wasn’t enough. The deed was done and the Lord’s will was done, though not yet all the way fully, because now we have to see the course of this whole thing.

One tidbit: “Now these are the generations of Esau, who is Edom.” Esau is Edom.

Edom was an ancient kingdom stretching across the area south of present-day Israel, Jordan and Palestine, where all that is going on over there right now. Once pushed out of their territory, they settled during the Persian period in the southern hills of Judea, down to north of Beersheba. There they appeared under a Greek form of their old name, Idumaeans, and their land was called Idumaea, a name used in the Hellenistic and Roman times and in the New Testament. The Treasury in Mount Seir was an Edomite stronghold.

What we just read in Genesis 27 is the beginning of Esau’s perpetual hatred.

sense.text: So who did God choose? When they that dwelt upon the earth multiplied and became a great people, “they began again to be more ungodly than the first.” These are the wicked, from between the sons of God and the sons of the wicked; they multiplied so heavily that the Most High had to flood the earth and get rid of them.

“Now when they lived so wickedly before thee, thou didst choose thee a man from among them, whose name was Abraham.” “Him thou lovedst, and unto him only thou shewedst thy will”, and made an everlasting covenant with him, “promising him that thou wouldest never forsake his seed”, because Abraham was a friend of God.

“And unto him thou gavest Isaac, and unto Isaac also thou gavest Jacob and Esau.” Now we are talking about Jacob and Esau. “As for Jacob, thou didst choose him to thee, and put by Esau: and so Jacob became a great multitude.” That is us. The blessing went to Jacob; God chose Jacob. That is what he meant when he said the elder shall serve the younger: the younger is Jacob, and the younger is the stronger one. It was all prophesied.

precepts.why:
Paul goes back to the same birth. “For this is the word of promise, At this time will I come, and Sara shall have a son. And not only this; but when Rebecca also had conceived by one, even by our father Isaac; (For the children being not yet born”

A lot of people ask, how can God just choose like that? Because he’s God, damn it. He’s God. The hell’s wrong with you? God does what he does, because he’s God. You are going to start asking questions about being politically correct, saying you don’t think that’s correct? The hell with you. God does what he does, and that is it.

“Neither having done any good or evil”: these babies did nothing good and nothing wrong. They were babies, floating in the water in their mother’s womb, doing nothing wrong, except fighting. “That the purpose of God according to election might stand, not of works, but of him that calleth”: he chooses whatever he wants. I do what I want; I am God.

“It was said unto her, The elder shall serve the younger.” It says unto her, not unto him: God told Rebecca how he wanted this to go down. “As it is written, Jacob have I loved, but Esau have I hated.”

So it is not because of anything good or evil that was done. It is through election: God elected Jacob; he wanted it to go down that way. Everybody else that doesn’t understand that, kick rocks. Take it up with God. This is what God already had written. If you don’t like what’s written, don’t read. Put your eyes out. Go play in traffic. Nobody cares.

sense.text:
“I have loved you, saith the Lord. Yet ye say, Wherein hast thou loved us?” A lot of us are praying to the Lord and none of our prayers are being answered, or so we think. Look at what is happening in the world: police brutality, ICE; on a global scale, the things going on in Sudan; the Jones Act in Puerto Rico and the massacres in Ponce and Utuado; the atrocities in the Congo under Belgium; Shark Island in Namibia; and now Epstein Island, drug trafficking and human trafficking. Our children are getting shot in their beds, revolutionaries are put to death for being revolutionary, and we are getting destroyed fighting for human rights. How the hell does God love us?

All these things have to happen. While they happen we are supposed to be going to the Lord, repenting, and looking in our book to make sure we are doing what God says. We are in the condition we are in today because we broke God’s commandments.

“Was not Esau Jacob’s brother? saith the Lord”: Esau is Jacob’s brother, the eldest. He should have had all the blessings, but God did not set it up that way. He set it up so that you get the blessings forever. And you say I don’t love you?

The only reason we say God doesn’t love us is our current condition: living paycheck to paycheck, the paycheck cut harder than it should be, held back by child support or divorce. I’m keeping the commandments, so how does God love me? You are doing your best, but just because you figured out you have to keep the commandments does not give you the right to the blessings right now. You have to pay. “Yet I loved Jacob.”

“And I hated Esau”, because he did God wrong: he despised his birthright, he sold it, and he went after us. “And laid his mountains and his heritage waste for the dragons of the wilderness”: everything that belongs to Esau is going to be destroyed. That is what God said.

“Whereas Edom saith, We are impoverished, but we will return and build the desolate places”: they were impoverished. We drove them into the Caucasus Mountains. But they rebuilt, came back, and now they are the superpower in the world, and they became that superpower by abusing their power, to the point where we see all the garbage in the world today.

“They shall build”, according to the blessing Isaac gave him, “but I will throw down.” That is the hand betwixt the heel: God makes sure the new kingdom that comes is under his son Christ, and Jacob will follow Christ, and that will be the kingdom forever. That is how he loves us.

“They shall call them, The border of wickedness”: they have the border between Canada and Mexico, and they are wicked between those borders. “The people against whom the Lord hath indignation for ever”: God hates these people forever.

“The vision of Obadiah. Thus saith the Lord God concerning Edom”. Obadiah is one sheet, one chapter. “Arise ye, and let us rise up against her in battle”: we are going into battle with Edom, but the battle is of the Lord.

“Behold, I have made thee small among the heathen: thou art greatly despised.” Esau is greatly despised: the title of this class. Why would anybody hate Esau? They seem really nice. They say good morning, good afternoon, good evening; sometimes they give you food, advice, a motivational speech. But they are greatly despised. They are small among the heathen because they don’t do things the way everybody else does; they march to the beat of their own drum and don’t give a damn about anything.

Here is why. On June 18, 1452, Pope Nicholas V issued the papal bull Dum Diversas, the first of the documents that make up the doctrine of discovery. It gave King Alfonso V of Portugal permission to invade, search out, capture, vanquish and subdue all Saracens and pagans and other enemies of Christ, to take their kingdoms, dominions and goods, and to reduce their persons to perpetual slavery. Saracen at first meant the Arabian tribes, but it went on to mean anybody who was not European. Perpetual slavery is like perpetual hatred, everlasting: rob us while they put us in chains. Romanus Pontifex came right after it, saying the same thing about perpetual slavery, and amplified it.

We went to Puerto Rico, with Captain Zefaniah and the men who deal with Puerto Rico directly, and met a 97-year-old man, the last survivor of the Puerto Rican Nationalist Party, who knew Pedro Albizu Campos personally. He is called a terrorist and a communist, but all he loved was his people. That frail man is called a terrorist and a communist, and they are going to say the same thing about us. In the library there they found the actual ID cards of the slaves on the island. Puerto Ricans are black.

The Russian propaganda posters in the Wayland Rudd Collection show it too: Lumumba carrying Africa in his heart; a brother punching the colonizer who holds money in one hand and a whip in the other; colonialism is doomed; colonizers must answer, caught red-handed murdering people; freedom to all the peoples of Africa, which is freedom to all the peoples of the Israelites. One shows the white man with the whip, then the black man holding the whip: they colonize our minds, and we become the taskmasters and managers over our own, no different than in the time of Moses. Colonialism will be doomed only when we wake up and realize we have been colonized, and what has been colonized is our minds and our attitude toward each other. Our soul has not been colonized; it should be colonized by the Most High God.

While Cold War America taught us that Russia was the evil empire, Russia was drawing what was happening over here.

The Utuado uprising of October 30, 1950 was a revolt against the United States government in Puerto Rico, with revolts in San Juan, Mayagüez, Arecibo, Ponce, Peñuelas and Adjuntas. Puerto Rico was in shambles: the Spanish wrecked it, then the United States did, cutting the Puerto Rican peso to half its worth so people lost their hard-earned savings overnight. The Nationalist Party was formed in 1922. Pedro Albizu Campos, the first Puerto Rican graduate of Harvard Law School, educated and sharp, believed Puerto Rico should be an independent nation, even if it took armed confrontation. The US-appointed governor Blanton Winship and Colonel Riggs applied harsh repression, and Albizu Campos and the party’s leaders were jailed in La Princesa and then in the federal prison in Atlanta. The party split, as there have always been splits among the Israelites, someone thinking he can do better. Stop hating and start participating.

The Jones Act requires that goods carried by water between US ports go on ships built, flagged, owned and crewed by Americans. The merchant seamen got no veterans’ benefits. The president waives it for fuel prices, not out of the kindness of his heart: Puerto Rico is a cash cow, and the people pay the price. The oil blockade on Cuba, ninety miles away, cripples life there. In the 1950s racism was woven into every part of life, and black travelers needed the Green Book to find where they could be safe. This is why Esau is greatly despised.

“The pride of thine heart hath deceived thee”: the pride of Esau’s heart has deceived him. How did God make Esau small among the heathen? They made so much noise and drew out so much blood that nobody wants to deal with America.

“Thou that dwellest in the clefts of the rock, whose habitation is high”: the clefts of the rock are the governments, the high places, the skyscrapers, all the richness and fatness of the earth that Esau lives in. They have the whole planet on lock. “That saith in his heart, Who shall bring me down to the ground?” They had their money, the Renaissance, Dum Diversas and Romanus Pontifex, and they put us all through slavery.

The Belgian atrocities show it. The Force Publique was the army of the Congo Free State and the Belgian Congo from 1885 to 1960, set up on Leopold II’s orders, and it did much damage there. The picture of the white man standing by a black boy whose hand was cut off is a perfect example: who is going to bring this white man down? I have power over black people; I can cut their hands off, and they will stand next to me comfortably and go do more work for me with one hand, with a smile on their face. They mixed black soldiers in under European officers: they were manipulating us to fight their battles. The Congolese man Nsala looked at the severed hand and foot of his five-year-old daughter, killed and cannibalized by the Force Publique in 1904. They say the force was a mixture of white and black, but we don’t eat our own. The white man does.

“Though thou exalt thyself as the eagle, and though thou set thy nest among the stars”: that is space travel. They set their nest among the stars with the Hubble and their satellites, which literally look like nests. They think they are above the Lord. You can exalt yourself like the eagle, but you are not the eagle and you are not God. The Susan B. Anthony coin of 1981 shows it: the eagle has landed, with branches, nesting on the moon, the earth in the background.

“Thence will I bring thee down, saith the Lord”: you are going to be taken down from your high habitation, your clefts of the rock.

“If thieves came to thee, if robbers by night, (how art thou cut off!) would they not have stolen till they had enough?” People who steal, steal to have enough. Esau is greatly despised because they continue to steal and steal and steal.

“If the grapegatherers came to thee, would they not leave some grapes?” The law says to leave grapes around the outskirts of the field for the poor, the poor of our people.

Read it with the exclamation point: “How are the things of Esau searched out! how are his hidden things sought up!” We are going to find out, going back in time.

The seal of the Spanish Inquisition, the first seat of the Inquisition in Seville: the Dominican friar Alonso de Ojeda convinced Queen Isabella of the need for an Inquisition, and Pope Gregory IX had already set up a pontifical Inquisition through the bull Excommunicamus. They prosecuted anyone found Judaizing or Moorish, and Judaizing and Moorish means doing anything that has to do with the Israelites.

The exorcist film puts it in a priest’s mouth: from the time the friar was possessed in 1475, everything after is the work of the devil. Everything from Dum Diversas on, and even before it, everything to do with the Vatican church, including the establishment of Christianity, is of the devil. The early church was of the Israelites. When Rome, Edom, Esau, Idumea came into power, they took it over, made the Renaissance, and changed the Sabbath to Sunday. They put a portion of what they did in a horror film so that it would sound crazy and you would disavow it. But we pause and look it up: Dum Diversas, Romanus Pontifex, the slavery. The devil is Esau. The white man is the devil.

precepts.why:
With the slavery pictures rolling: “And the Lord shall bring thee into Egypt again with ships”. This is how it happened: we went into Egypt again, slavery again, with ships, cargo slave ships.

“By the way whereof I spake unto thee, Thou shalt see it no more again”: you will never see Israel again, because we broke God’s commandments. So now we have to go through this, and it is all part of Esau’s blessing as well. We broke God’s commandments, and God put Esau over us.

“And there ye shall be sold unto your enemies”: not only to the white man but to other nations, through the transatlantic slave trade, the trans-Saharan slave trade, all the other slave trades and the Silk Road. We ended up in China, in Japan, as far as the Philippine Islands; parts of Issachar are in the Philippines, and Puerto Ricans, the tribe of Ephraim, are in Hawaii.

“For bondmen and bondwomen”: slave men and slave women. “And no man shall buy you”: no revolutionary will save us, no matter how eloquently they speak or how hard they fight.

J. Edgar Hoover, that bastard, said the number one threat to America was the organization of Negroes. When we started to build, as in Tulsa and Rosewood, they cut us out. That is part of the curses: “Therefore shalt thou serve thine enemies”. That is not a suggestion; it is part of the curses. “Which the Lord shall send against thee”: it was God that sent these people against us, “in hunger, and in thirst, and in nakedness, and in want of all things”.

“And he shall put a yoke of iron upon thy neck, until he have destroyed thee.” Now we are so destroyed that we can’t even organize. As Godfrey said, we can’t even organize crime. But that does not mean we can’t organize the truth. To hell with organized crime: we are organizing the truth, an organized nation, looking for like-minded brothers and sisters willing to wake up, keep God’s commandments and see this thing to the end.

The movements tried. The Greensboro Four planned their sit-in knowing they would be denied service, and it spread to 55 cities in 13 states; SNCC organized the Freedom Rides and the March on Washington. When doing things peacefully failed, the Black Panthers bore arms as the law allowed, and they didn’t like black people having guns. Then the Young Lords, and blacks, Latinos and Native Americans together, which is exactly what Hoover did not want. Huey Newton said the oppressor must be harassed until his doom, that the enslaved have always outnumbered the enslavers. But what was missing from the Black Panthers, the Young Lords and the American Indian Movement? The Bible. Had they had the Bible, we would probably be in the kingdom by now.
